subject.title: fix(openai-responses): recover streamed invalid_encrypted_content via drain-level retry (#95441)

question: After the branch is rebased, should the generic Responses drain retry require live provider or deployment proof before merge, or should maintainers explicitly override that gate and accept it as defense in depth beside the Copilot-only provider-boundary fix?
rationale: The code and mocked gates support correctness, but only maintainers can accept the session-continuity tradeoff and waive the repository's external-PR real-setup proof requirement for a provider and session-state change.

options.title: Require live retry proof
options.body: Require redacted output from the rebased PR head showing a real streamed encrypted-content rejection retries once and yields one assistant reply without duplicate lifecycle events.

options.title: Override for defense in depth
options.body: Explicitly accept the mock-backed transport proof and land the generic retry alongside the Copilot provider-boundary prevention path.

options.title: Prefer provider-boundary only
options.body: Pause this PR and first land or reject https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95493, then reassess whether generic drain recovery adds enough value.

recommendation.title: Require live retry proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted output from the rebased PR head showing a real streamed encrypted-content rejection retries once and yields one assistant reply without duplicate lifecycle events.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the one-shot OpenAI Responses retry behavior introduced in steipete's merged transport change and concerns its intended permanent scope.
